wins.text: Q3 revenue of $57B, up 62% YoY and record sequential growth of $10B (+22% QoQ)
Data center revenue hit a record $51.2B, up 66% YoY; networking revenue of $8.2B surged 162% YoY
Non-GAAP gross margins of 73.6% exceeded guidance, with Q4 guided to 75% — exiting the year in mid-70s as promised
Visibility to $500B in Blackwell and Rubin revenue from start of 2025 through end of calendar 2026, with upside from new deals (Anthropic 1GW commitment, KSA/HUMAIN 400K-600K GPUs)
Gaming revenue of $4.3B up 30% YoY; Professional Visualization revenue of $760M up 56% YoY (record); Automotive revenue of $592M up 32% YoY

risks.text: H20 China sales were approximately $50M — sizable purchase orders never materialized due to geopolitical issues and competitive market; no China data center compute revenue assumed in Q4 guidance
Input costs rising into FY2027, creating gross margin pressure; management guiding to 'work to hold' margins in mid-70s rather than expand them
Supply chain constraints across power, financing, memory, and foundry capacity cited as real bottlenecks given unprecedented growth rate
Inventory grew 32% QoQ and supply commitments increased 63% sequentially, reflecting significant forward bets on demand that must materialize
Hyperscaler customer concentration risk — top CSPs represent the dominant share of data center revenue, with aggregate CapEx plans of ~$600B that could be revised

guidance_items.detail: Q4 revenue guided to $65B +/- 2%, implying ~14% sequential growth; well above Q3's $57B
Q4 non-GAAP gross margins guided to 75% +/- 50bps, up from 73.6% in Q3; FY2027 target to hold in mid-70s
Q4 GAAP/non-GAAP other income ~$500M; tax rate 17% +/- 1%
Supply commitments increased 63% sequentially, signaling aggressive forward investment in supply chain for anticipated demand

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Whether supply can realistically catch up with demand over the next 12-18 months
Capital allocation priorities — buybacks vs. ecosystem investments vs. balance sheet given ~$500B in projected free cash flow
Competitive threat from AI ASICs/custom XPUs from hyperscalers and whether GPU architecture dominance is at risk
